nameOrigin.text: The townsite was first platted as Fremont; postal officials refused that name because Colorado already had a Fremont, and the name Cripple Creek was then suggested and approved.

founded.text: A settlement of tents and cabins grew up in the fall of 1891 and the landowners platted 80 acres as a townsite

timeline.text: Bob Womack found gold ore in Poverty Gulch and filed a mining claim, the start of the last gold rush in Colorado.
Two fires four days apart in April destroyed most of the city, which was rebuilt in brick and stone.
Teller County was formed and Cripple Creek was voted the county seat.
Cripple Creek was named a National Historic Landmark.
Legalized gambling came to Cripple Creek.
